report.answer_text:
In its June 23, 2025 “First Look” release, the Vera C. Rubin Observatory showed a detailed composite of the Trifid and Lagoon nebulae, revealing faint clouds of gas and dust, and a sweeping view of the Virgo Cluster region, filled with galaxies. The release also highlighted 2,104 previously unknown asteroids detected in its initial observations. (nsf.gov)
Its flagship project is the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), a 10-year survey that repeatedly images the southern night sky every few nights. By comparing those images, astronomers can track moving objects such as asteroids, spot changes such as supernova explosions, and study dark matter and dark energy. (nationalacademies.org)
